name: Overwatch 2
short_description: Team hero shooter with a cast of very different, very readable characters.
sources: oracle study 2026-10-23 (public knowledge, no store fetch, no game files)
summary: Team hero shooter with a cast of very different, very readable characters.

identity.core_loop: Pick a hero, push or hold the objective with your team, use abilities and ultimates, swap heroes when needed.
identity.ui_and_game_feel: Snappy and readable; each hero feels different from the first frame you hold them.

hud_coverage.method: Oracle study from public knowledge of the game, in our own words; not yet measured on capture

information_grammar.note: Heroes read by silhouette and voice lines; ultimates are called out loud; overlay for health, ammo and abilities.

identity.art_direction: Stylised PBR with bright saturated colour, clean shapes and strong silhouettes.

rendering.source: derived from the art note by rendering_notes.RULES

tricks: Hand-keyed heroes with strong poses and silhouettes; personality even in first-person arms
First-person and third-person animations are separate sets, each tuned for its camera
Big anticipation and snappy recovery so abilities read across a busy fight
motion.lesson: Key the characters for pose and silhouette first; give the first-person hands their own personality.

sources.title: GDC Vault: The Animation Pipeline of Overwatch
Game Anim: The first person animation of Overwatch (Matthew Boehm, GDC 2017)
Inven Global: how Overwatch's first-person animation breathed life into heroes

motion.source: oracle motion study 2026-10-23 (public talks, interviews and breakdowns; no game files)

identity.audio_mood: Voice barks for every key moment; distinct audio signature per hero.
identity.lessons_for_abbies_world: Each character's personality lives in how they move and stand, even in first person. Silhouette and pose first.
